clinician.trajectory_summary: An 86-year-old female with type 2 diabetes presented with right-sided hemiparesis and Gerstmann syndrome symptoms (finger agnosia, agraphia, acalculia, right–left disorientation). A brain CT scan on admission revealed a chronic subdural hematoma (Markwalder grade 2, 1.5 cm, hypodense) on the left frontal and parietal lobes, without mass effect or subfalcine herniation. A follow-up CT scan the next day showed signs of hematoma resorption and decreased thickness. At discharge, the right hemiparesis had slightly remitted (MRC 4/5), but Gerstmann syndrome symptoms showed no improvement or worsening. Fludrocortisone was prescribed for the intracranial hematoma.

A follow-up CT scan showed signs of resorption and a decrease in the hematoma’s thickness.
At discharge, right hemiparesis improved, but Gerstmann syndrome symptoms showed no improvement or worsening.
Fludrocortisone was prescribed for the intracranial hematoma at discharge.
